Use case: stylized-concept. Create ONE finished full-bleed landscape illustration for a bilingual Stardew Valley farmhouse-upgrade blog. Canvas: widescreen 16:9, target 2048x1152. Visual language: authentic cozy 16-bit farming RPG pixel art, like a lovingly crafted in-game environment; crisp square pixel clusters on a consistent pixel grid, deliberately stepped outlines, restrained dithering and a limited harmonious palette. Flat 2D top-down three-quarter game view, readable tile geometry, warm honey timber, terracotta roof, cream walls, lush sage and forest greens, warm late-afternoon light and soft purple pixel shadows. Rich handcrafted environmental details with a clear focal point and uncluttered composition. Keep all important subjects away from extreme edges. Render a complete scene, not a poster, diagram, triptych or collage. Absolutely no visible text, letters, digits, labels, UI, HUD, menus, price cards, arrows, panels, logos, signatures, watermarks or pseudo-writing. Avoid blurry antialiased edges, gradients, painterly brushwork, photorealism, glossy 3D and modern vector illustration. Opaque background.
Scene: a beautifully expanded wooden farmhouse centered in a small lush farm clearing, welcoming front porch, flower pots, chimney, shutters and warm windows. A winding earth path leads to the front door. Small neat crop beds and a low wooden fence frame the foreground; leafy trees frame the background. A tidy stack of pale construction planks and a few darker hardwood logs rest beside the house, suggesting an upgrade just completed. The farmhouse is the large unmistakable hero, filling most of the composition. Quiet, inviting, warm and lived-in. No character is needed. This is an atmospheric original editorial illustration, not an exact screenshot or a canonical floor plan.

The carpenter is a tiny clearly drawn farming-game sprite with auburn hair, work shirt and tool belt, raising a small hammer toward a solid timber beam. A second small farmer sprite stands nearby watching. Simple timber scaffolding along one side of the farmhouse, a neat stack of planks and logs, a toolbox, fence and dirt path make the task legible. The finished main part of the house remains cozy and welcoming, with windows and flowers, while the side extension is visibly under construction.
